clue.text: Previous quality reportedly drawn from stone

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is spoken, so the written answer is what it sounds like

parts.note: previous is EX (a former one) and quality is CALIBRE, giving ex-calibre

explanation.surface: Someone's former quality, by the sound of it, has been drawn out of a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur proved his right to the throne by drawing the sword from the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend the young Arthur pulls this sword from a stone, proving himself king.

clue.text: Part of phone for a note each — that's about right

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes A to G

indicators.note: about means the word for each goes round the letter for right

parts.note: apiece means each, as in a pound apiece

explanation.surface: A phone part costs one note each, which seems about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's about right' sounds like approval of a price; 'about' actually puts R inside APIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: The earpiece is the component of a telephone handset held against the ear.

clue.text: Fool gets the chop

definitions.meaning: a ... chop is a cut of lamb from the loin end

explanation.surface: A fool is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the chop' reads as being sacked; here 'chop' is the meat, as in a chump chop, a butcher's cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Chump is both a colloquial word for an idiot and the name of a thick cut of meat.

clue.text: One having affinity with Viviane in the 6 20 tales had problem with fan

definitions.text: One having affinity with Viviane in the 6 20 tales
definitions.meaning: Viviane is the Lady of the Lake in the King Arthur stories; Windermere is England's largest lake, so its lady is akin to her
Wilde's comedy ... Fan turns on the trouble caused by her fan

explanation.surface: A character linked with Viviane in the Arthurian stories was troubled by a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Windermere is a lake in the English Lake District, so a lady of it parallels the Lady of the Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Oscar Wilde's play has a lake in her name and a fan that causes scandal.

clue.text: Brazier's work is weird

indicators.note: work signals that the letters of the brazier are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word brazier, its possessive ending giving no letter

explanation.surface: A metalworker's handiwork looks strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre and weird are synonyms meaning strikingly odd or unusual.

clue.text: Tick off agent and don't stand still

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
to rove is to wander about rather than stay put

explanation.surface: Telling off an agent for not standing still.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick someone off is to reprove or scold them.

clue.text: Family enclosed courtyard at old city, one scheduled for a comeback?

parts.note: kin means family, relatives
a garth is an enclosed yard or garden, as in a cloister garth
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A family's walled courtyard in an ancient city awaits someone due to return.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend calls Arthur 'the once and future king', who will come again when Britain needs him.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend holds that this king sleeps and is destined to return, so he is due to make a comeback.

clue.text: Within limits of popular seating for artists

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sofa is a piece of seating
RA is a Royal Academician, so artists are RAs

explanation.surface: A fashionable couch made for painters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to the extent that, limiting a statement to a certain range.

clue.text: Extractor of fragments more important in utterance

indicators.note: in utterance signals that the word is spoken and the answer is spelt the way it sounds

parts.note: greater means more important

explanation.surface: Something that pulls out fragments matters more when spoken of.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen grater shreds food into small fragments, so it extracts bits from a block.

clue.text: 6 20's parent, topless Reformer and writer — are they never going to stop?

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the reformer's name is removed

parts.note: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation
a pen is a writing instrument

parts.words: are they never going to stop?
parts.note: a complaint that things drag on, continuing tediously

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint about a Reformer and an author who go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes the first letter off LUTHER, leaving UTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legends Uther Pendragon is the king who fathered Arthur.

clue.text: 6 20's supporters 'adn't gone astray in currency

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters are placed inside the currency

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

indicators.note: gone astray signals that the letters of the dropped-aitch word wander into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word as printed, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Arthur's backers, in Cockney speech, had not gone missing in the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adn't is Cockney for hadn't, its dropped aitch marked by the apostrophe; 'gone astray' shuffles its letters and 'in' places them inside the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The knights of the Round Table were Arthur's companions and loyal supporters.

clue.text: Guerrilla strike at island's volunteers

parts.note: to zap is to hit or strike
I for island plus the 's
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Guerrillas launch an attack on an island's volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Zapatistas are Mexican guerrilla fighters named after the revolutionary Emiliano Zapata.

clue.text: Ruling confined captive queen

parts.note: in, as in kept in, means confined
POW is a prisoner of war, a captive
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruler keeps a queen locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A party that is ruling holds office, which the phrase describes.

clue.text: Georgia artist spoke effectively, according to some

indicators.note: some signals only part of the phrase is taken, letters sitting within it

explanation.surface: Some say a painter from Georgia was a persuasive speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgia' looks like the country, but it is the painter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The American painter of flowers and desert landscapes was named Georgia, so she is the Georgia artist.

clue.text: Sergeant at penal settlement is hot stuff

indicators.note: at means the sergeant is placed after, located at the settlement

parts.note: Cayenne in French Guiana was the site of a notorious French penal colony
Sgt Pepper, from the Beatles album title

explanation.surface: A military sergeant posted to a prison colony is a fiery character.
explanation.definitionFit: This ground chilli is a spice known for its heat, so it is hot stuff.

clue.text: Sailing group in raised parking area keeping clutch out

indicators.note: keeping means the reversed parking spot holds the shuffled letters inside it
raised in a down answer means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a parking bay is a space for parking

indicators.note: out signals the letters of clutch are put out of order

explanation.surface: A sailing club gathers in a raised car park, avoiding the clutch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'raised' reads the parking word upwards; 'out' shuffles clutch, and 'keeping' holds those letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht club is an association of people who sail, a sailing group.

clue.text: Report of Pakistani province and European capital with characteristic manifestations

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular noun: a syndrome is a set of such signs taken together

indicators.note: report of signals the words are spoken, the answer spelt by their sound

parts.note: Sind is a province of Pakistan and Rome the capital of Italy, together SIND ROME

explanation.surface: An account of a Pakistani province and Rome shows typical signs.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a group of symptoms that together characterise a condition.

clue.text: With a sort of cough about, a beast of a crossing around Pole is naff

indicators.note: about signals that the cough word encloses the following pieces

parts.note: a chesty cough comes from the chest

indicators.note: around means the beast at the crossing is wrapped round the letter for the Pole

parts.note: a panda crossing was a type of British pedestrian crossing, and a panda is a beast
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A coughing creature at a crossing near the Pole is tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda crossing was a short-lived British push-button pedestrian crossing; 'around' wraps the beast round Pole, and 'about' wraps the cough round A plus that.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky or vulgar, the same sense as cheap and tawdry.

clue.text: A drop-in arranged for bosses

indicators.note: arranged signals the letters of the phrase are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A casual visit is set up for the managers.
explanation.definitionFit: Padroni is the Italian plural for masters or employers, used in English for bosses.

clue.text: Retribution for a bloomer with the wrong end

indicators.note: with the wrong end means the last letter of the flower is replaced by another

parts.note: nemesia is a flowering garden plant, so a bloomer

explanation.surface: Punishment for an error with the wrong ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a flower: NEMESIA with its final A replaced by S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is deserved punishment, named after the Greek goddess of retribution.

clue.text: See 6
Revised estimate of how long grass covered small boy …

indicators.note: covered means the plant word goes round the boy's name

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
Tim is a short form of Timothy, a boy's name

explanation.surface: Reeds grew over a little boy, and the timing was reassessed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retime something is to set a new estimate or schedule for its duration.

clue.text: … which could be as it should be

indicators.note: could be signals that the previous answer's letters may be rearranged

parts.note: which refers back to the answer of the previous clue

explanation.surface: Something that might be exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue; 'which' stands for its answer, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something merited is deserved, which is how things ought to be.

clue.text: See 10
Very amusing greeting to housekeeper's bills

parts.note: hi is a greeting
a lar is a Roman household god, keeper of the house, with possessive 's
IOUs are written promises to pay, bills

explanation.surface: A housekeeper's bills arrive with a cheery hello and much laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lares were Roman guardian spirits of the home, whence 'housekeeper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarious means extremely funny, very amusing.

clue.text: Merchant characters with mouth odour

definitions.note: plural phrase: Launcelot and his father old Gobbo share the surname

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Trading figures with bad breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant' is The Merchant of Venice, in which Launcelot Gobbo and his father appear.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, the clown Launcelot and his father bear this surname.

clue.text: Take decoration from garment

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take
the OBE is a British honour, a decoration

explanation.surface: Removing an ornament from a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' looks like a verb meaning remove; it is R, the prescription abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment.

clue.text: False quantity of captains in ceremonial dress

indicators.note: quantity of signals that only some of the letters of the phrase are taken, a run within it

explanation.surface: A number of captains in full uniform are false.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere means not genuine, false in feeling.
